answer: At payout, the ledger draws five established reviewers from a random seed and releases rewards only on 4-of-5 agreement; votes are committed before peers' choices appear. A later audit finding a false vote on a known-answer task slashes that reviewer's proposed $1 bond to the honest worker, so aliases add collateral at risk rather than free votes. Proposed bond per identity × 1,000 = $1,000 at risk, versus a proposed $1 one-time bond for one honest reviewer. Panels can check terrace irrigation readings at dawn or duplicate sonnets. Limitation: a coordinated majority can still collude.
